paper.title: Dynamic Regret for Non-Stationary Linear Bandits via Misspecification Reductions

settings.name_in_paper: Non-stationary linear bandits with general compact, adaptive non-anticipating decision sets
unmapped: Non-stationarity measured by path length P_T = sum_t ||theta_{t+1}-theta_t||_2 of an oblivious parameter sequence
The learner knows the path length P_T (used to tune the block length)
Decision sets may be adaptive but non-anticipating (depend on past history, fixed before current-round randomization)
settings.definition_quote:
Formally, consider an online decision-making problem over \(T\) rounds: at
each round \(t\), the learner observes a feasible decision set
\(\mathcal A_t\subseteq\mathbb R^d\), chooses an action
\(a_t\in\mathcal A_t\), and receives a reward with conditional mean
\(\langle a_t,\theta_t\rangle\), where \(\theta_t\) is the current reward
parameter. Following \citet{cheung2022hedging}, the non-stationarity of a
problem instance is measured by the path length of the reward-parameter
sequence, \(P_T:=\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}\|\theta_{t+1}-\theta_t\|_2\).

settings.definition_quote: we consider the K-armed contextual linear-bandit specialization under an oblivious adversary, where A_t={x_t(i):i∈[K]} at each round ... The sequence (A_t,θ_t)_{t=1}^T is fixed before the learner's randomization.

settings.name_in_paper: K-armed contextual linear bandits with path-length constraint (lower bound)
unmapped: Non-stationarity measured by path length budget P_T of the parameter sequence
settings.definition_quote:
Consider \(K\)-armed contextual linear bandits with \(K\ge2\) actions per
round, \(\|x_{t,a}\|_2\le1\), \(\|\theta_t\|_2\le1\), and path-length $\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}\|\theta_{t+1}-\theta_t\|_2\le P_T$.

source.label: thm:known-path-dynamic-regret
source.quote: Suppose Assumptions~\ref{ass:subgaussian-noise} and~\ref{ass:bounded-rewards} hold. Suppose the parameter path (θ_t) is fixed before interaction begins, has known path length P_T, and is independent of the learner's randomization. The decision sets may be adaptive but non-anticipating. Run Algorithm~\ref{alg:restart-misspec-adaptive} with block length Δ = ... Then Reg_T ≤ \widetilde O( d\sqrt T + L^{1/3}d^{5/6}T^{2/3}P_T^{1/3}).

results.notes: Dynamic regret defined in expectation against per-round optimal action under current parameter. Block-level Lemma (thm:block-mis-adaptive) not recorded separately; it is the misspecified block guarantee O~(d sqrt n + sqrt d n eps).

source.label: prop:finite-k-lower-bound
source.quote: Consider K-armed contextual linear bandits with K≥2 actions per round, ||x_{t,a}||_2≤1, ||θ_t||_2≤1, and path-length ... ≤P_T. Let Γ_{d,K} be the maximum of (d\min\{K,d\})^{1/6} and (\min\{d,\lfloor\log_2K\rfloor\})^{2/3}. Then the minimax dynamic regret is at least Ω(\sqrt{dT}\vee P_T^{1/3}T^{2/3}Γ_{d,K}). The lower bound holds for obliviously chosen contexts and parameter sequences.

results.notes: Only a proof sketch is given. Noise model of the hard instance not explicitly stated; assumed sub-Gaussian as in the setting.
